data.narrative:
Electric Era is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Quincy Lee that has raised $11.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine frontier-energy peers: one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A stage-progression methodology provides the primary valuation anchor. Using the $11.5M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $23M. This approach assumes Electric Era will progress to the next financing stage at market-standard terms.

A peer-median comparison approach was not applicable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none qualified as sufficiently narrow comparables on stage, funding round proximity, or valuation tier. Applying an all-sector median without this filtering would introduce material noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $20M (low) to $26M (high), with a median of $23M. This analysis rests on a single quantitative method; range width reflects inherent uncertainty in frontier-stage climate tech, which operates in emerging markets with unproven unit economics. Key uncertainties include technology validation timelines, regulatory environment shifts, and capital efficiency relative to peers.
